interest: This file provides a revealing perspective on wartime U.S. State Department internal deliberations surrounding state-level alien land laws, particularly Oregon's enforcement of escheat proceedings against Japanese property owners during World War II. It illustrates the practical legal dilemmas faced by federal officials, such as Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth, in determining whether to invoke the abrogated 1911 U.S.-Japan Treaty of Commerce and Navigation and how to advise state boards without endorsing questionable legal premises. Additionally, the documents illuminate wartime diplomatic mechanisms, showing how the State Department considered using Switzerland as the protecting power to ascertain Japanese domestic statutes, as well as early hemispheric security concerns regarding Japanese immigrant communities in Peru.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.52, 'Japan, Lands') spans April 20, 1942 to May 12, 1943, and documents wartime legal and policy questions concerning Japanese landholding and real property rights. The opening document is a 1942 cross-reference sheet concerning a Peruvian request for Japanese-speaking agents to monitor Japanese colonists in Peru. The remainder of the file consists of internal State Department memoranda from April and May 1943 prompted by an inquiry from Mr. Griffith and the State Land Board of Oregon regarding the ownership of real property by Japanese subjects and Oregon escheat statutes. Officials from the Legal Adviser's Office (Green H. Hackworth), the Treaty Division (W. V. Whittington), and the Special Division (W. Franklin) debate whether to mention the abrogated 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan, consider how to address Japanese domestic real estate laws, and suggest obtaining legal texts from Tokyo through the Swiss Government acting as the protecting power.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet regarding a Peruvian government request for Japanese-speaking agents in connection with the Japanese colony in Peru.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of American Republics
subfiles.summary: A Department of State cross-reference sheet indexing a memorandum of April 20, 1942, originally filed under 894.20223/127. It records a conversation with the Peruvian Minister of Finance, who requested the loan of one or more Japanese-speaking agents to assist Peru with its Japanese colony. The paper was cross-referenced to decimal file 894.52 under the subject of Japanese land and community matters.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japanese Colony in Peru

subfiles.about: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth's critique of a draft reply to the State Land Board of Oregon regarding Japanese property rights.
subfiles.summary: Legal Adviser Green H. Hackworth comments critically on a draft letter to the State Land Board of Oregon. He questions why the Department would discuss or enclose the terminated 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation with Japan, pointing out that even when in force, the treaty never granted Japanese subjects the right to own real property. Hackworth also recommends deleting standard boilerplate paragraphs on alien land rights to focus strictly on the Department's stance regarding the Board's proposed escheat action.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Green H. Hackworth on Draft Reply to Oregon State Land Board

subfiles.about: Treaty Division memorandum by W. V. Whittington discussing modifications to a draft letter to Mr. Griffith concerning Japanese land laws and Oregon escheat proceedings.
subfiles.summary: W. V. Whittington of the Treaty Division writes to Mr. Barnes concerning revisions to a draft letter for Mr. Griffith. He addresses the Special Division's concern that the Department should not disclaim knowledge of Japanese real property laws, while noting that Japanese domestic laws have no legal bearing on Oregon's escheat statutes. Whittington suggests deleting the penultimate paragraph admitting lack of information and appending clarifying language to the preceding paragraph based on an attached draft.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from W. V. Whittington to Mr. Barnes Regarding Letter to Mr. Griffith

subfiles.about: Special Division memorandum proposing to obtain Japanese alien real property laws via the Swiss Government.
subfiles.summary: W. Franklin of the Special Division expresses reluctance to admit in correspondence that the State Department lacks information concerning Japanese laws governing alien ownership of real property. The memorandum proposes requesting this legal information from Japan through the Swiss Government, which was representing American interests as protecting power during the war. It also refers the reader to an underlying memorandum on the subject by Mr. Smith.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Special Division on Japanese Alien Real Property Laws
